key_insight: DrugHarness is an evolvable agent framework that learns when and how to reuse scientific skills for computational drug discovery, improving performance across screening, optimization, and constrained design.
engineering_relevance: It provides a practical architecture for scientific agents that combines composable tool execution, evidence-linked skill induction, and review-based skill admission for more reliable drug-design workflows.
method: Integrates 80+ biomedical/scientific operations with task-specific code and artifact tracking.
Induces conditional skills from execution trajectories plus outcome feedback, including applicability conditions and supporting evidence.
Uses an independent review agent to verify, trial, and admit candidate skills before reuse in future tasks.
evidence_signal: On MolBench and SMDD-Bench, DrugHarness outperforms prior baselines, including a 10.8-point gain in affinity-comparison accuracy and a 55% increase in mean top-three active hits without evolution.
watch_item: Performance gains depend on robust source verification and targeted trial execution, so skill admission may be sensitive to noisy evidence or incomplete task coverage.
paper_title: DrugHarness: An Evolvable Agent Harness for Computational Drug Discovery
